blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What your BSc Agriculture seat really is

rows: ICAR quota seat (national exam)

CUET (ICAR-UG) merit rank, then ICAR counselling. The bulletin says the exam covers 20 percent of university seats, and 100 percent at six named institutions. There is no direct nomination without the exam.

Class 12 needs at least three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture, with 50 percent marks (40 percent for SC, ST and PwBD). Many universities add an age cap, such as 22 years at one and 25 years at another.
State quota seat at a state agricultural university
The university or state runs its own admission process for the remaining seats. Rules and subject lists differ by state.
Ask the university for last year's cut-off and fee. We found no reliable national fee table, so we print none.
Private college affiliated to a university
Admission follows the college and its university. ICAR accreditation is a separate step that ICAR gives to colleges.
Check the college on the current ICAR list before you pay. Student Q&A pages say employers weigh ICAR status differently, so read the notice for each post you want.

blocks.heading: BSc Agriculture Career Options
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Twelve BSc Agriculture career options, ordered by growth room

rows: 1. Farm advisory, soil and crop data services Scalable
Farmers, FPOs, input companies and food processors pay for a soil report, a crop plan or a field visit note. They trust a farm that improved and a farmer who refers you.
BSc Agriculture is enough to start. Add soil testing know-how, a spreadsheet habit and a local language you speak well. No exam needed.
2. Agri-input shop (seed, fertiliser, crop protection) Scalable with a business layer
Farmers who buy every season. They trust a shopkeeper who gives the right dose and stays honest when a crop fails.

Licence rules apply. The Assam licence form asks for a degree in Agriculture or Science for a pesticide licence, and the MANAGE DAESI diploma is the route for dealers without one in some states. Check your state.
3. FPO manager or FPO consultant Scalable with a business layer
The FPO's farmer members, plus government support and customers. Members trust honest accounts and a fair price on sale day.
BSc Agriculture plus accounts, group meetings and market linkage skills. Roles open through FPOs and the agencies that guide them.
4. Own farm or agri-enterprise (high-value crops, nursery, seed, processing) Scalable with a business layer
Traders, processors, retailers and direct customers. They trust quality that stays the same across batches and a supplier who delivers on time.
Land or a lease, capital and one crop or product you know well. A season working in someone else's unit comes first.
5. Drone and precision-farm services Scalable with a business layer
Farmers, FPOs and input companies pay for spraying, mapping or crop monitoring. They trust a clean job on their own field.
BSc Agriculture for crop and dose judgment, plus a certified remote pilot and a drone that meets DGCA rules. Check the current DGCA and agriculture ministry pages.
6. Natural farming inputs and training Scalable with a business layer
Farmers moving to natural farming, and the government mission that funds training and input centres. Farmers trust a plot that did well, not a brochure.
BSc Agriculture, or the newer BSc (Hons) Natural Farming. Hands-on practice in a working natural farm matters more than a certificate.
1. Farm advisory, soil and crop data services Scalable
Paid farm visits, a seasonal crop-plan package for one crop and one district, then a small advisory firm. The same skill sells to many clients.
2. Agri-input shop (seed, fertiliser, crop protection) Scalable with a business layer
Your own shop, then a second outlet, a farm-advice desk and custom crop packages. Credit given to farmers is the big risk.
3. FPO manager or FPO consultant Scalable with a business layer
Consulting for several FPOs at once: business plans, compliance help and market linkage. One FPO cannot pay a large salary, so the layer is the consulting.
4. Own farm or agri-enterprise (high-value crops, nursery, seed, processing) Scalable with a business layer
Value addition (grading, drying, packing), a brand, contract supply and a second product. Weather and price swings are real costs.
5. Drone and precision-farm services Scalable with a business layer
A spraying and mapping service across a cluster of villages, with trained pilots working for you. Equipment, batteries and season peaks set the limit.
6. Natural farming inputs and training Scalable with a business layer
A bio-input unit that sells ready-to-use inputs, plus paid training days. Details are in the business layers section.
IBPS Specialist Officer, Agriculture Field Officer
Four-year degree in agriculture or an allied subject; age 20 to 30. The page we read lists 370 posts after an update on 20 July 2026, with prelims, mains and interview.
Scale I basic pay Rs 48,480 a month, plus allowances set by each bank
NABARD Grade A (Rural Development Banking Service)

A bachelor's degree with 60 percent marks (55 percent for SC, ST and PwBD) and age 21 to 30, as summarised by coaching sites. The last round, notified 8 November 2025, listed 91 posts. We could not confirm which degrees the stream accepts.
Not confirmed from an official page, so none printed
State agriculture officer (Kerala example)
BSc Agriculture or Horticulture from a recognised university. One 100-mark online objective test of 90 minutes, then document checks.
Rs 55,200 to Rs 1,15,300 a month plus allowances
ICAR ARS scientist (ASRB combined exam)

Master's degree in the discipline (check the notice for discipline rules); age 21 to 32. The 2025 combined notice listed 582 posts in all, of which 458 were scientist posts. Stages: prelims, mains, interview.
Pay matrix Rs 57,700 to Rs 1,82,400 a month at entry level
ICAR JRF or SRF for a PhD

A relevant master's degree at 60 percent (55 percent for SC, ST and PwBD) per a guide we read; no age cap and no attempt limit there. The 2026 PG and PhD tests were held on 4 July 2026: 42,110 registered and 38,720 appeared.
Rs 31,000 a month for two years, Rs 35,000 in year three, plus Rs 10,000 a year for research costs
ICAR PG scholarship after the PG exam
BSc Agriculture holders sit the ICAR PG exam for an MSc seat at an agricultural university. The same exam took 28,303 test-takers in 2026.
Rs 12,640 a month for two years plus Rs 6,000 a year, per a guide we read
IBPS Specialist Officer, Agriculture Field Officer
48,480 x 12 = Rs 5,81,760 a year in basic pay alone. A coaching summary lists 310 posts for the 2025 round, so the count moves from year to year.
NABARD Grade A (Rural Development Banking Service)
91 posts for the whole country in one round. Read the NABARD notice for subject rules before you plan around it.
State agriculture officer (Kerala example)
55,200 x 12 = Rs 6,62,400 a year at the lowest step. Odisha listed 118 assistant agriculture officer posts in 2026, which shows how much counts differ by state.
ICAR ARS scientist (ASRB combined exam)
57,700 x 12 = Rs 6,92,400 a year at entry. ARS posts were 79 percent of the 582 in that notice, and the other 124 were SMS and technical officer posts.
ICAR JRF or SRF for a PhD
(31,000 x 12) + 10,000 = Rs 3,82,000 a year. That is 55 percent of the entry ARS figure above, and it buys training, not a post.
ICAR PG scholarship after the PG exam
12,640 x 24 = Rs 3,03,360 over the MSc. Check the official ICAR notice for the current rate.

rows: Spotting pests and stress from drone or satellite pictures
High. Platforms already flag problem patches.
Walking the field, finding the cause and telling the farmer what to do.
General crop advice by app or chat
High for standard advice on sowing, dose and weather.
Local soil, local seed, and the trust of a farmer who will act on it.
Writing reports, plans and FPO paperwork
Medium. Drafts come fast.
Checking every number, and knowing which scheme or rule applies.
Spraying and mapping
Medium. Drones take the hours spent walking and spraying.
Judging dose, timing and safety. The paid work moves to the person who runs the drones, which is the business layer.
Dealer, customer and farmer relationships
Low.
